summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia was admitted for evaluation of left-sided chest pain and shoulder discomfort. The pain was reproducible on palpation, with normal cardiac enzymes and EKG, leading to a diagnosis of costochondritis. Shoulder X-ray revealed degenerative changes with osteophytes causing impingement. She developed transient hyperglycemia due to missing a dose of Lantus insulin in the emergency department, which was corrected with bridging and resumption of her home regimen. A urine culture grew Staphylococcus aureus, sensitive to multiple antibiotics, though she lacked systemic symptoms, and no treatment was initiated during admission. She was discharged home after 48 hours on stable condition with NSAIDs for musculoskeletal pain, continued cardiac and diabetes medications, and instructions for outpatient follow-up.
